The ability of these systems to aid in creating new mathematical arguments and proof steps will become increasingly valuable. Mathematical problem-solving will continue to evolve due to the collaboration of AI and mathematics. Despite this, there will be limitations on the acceptance of AI systems in the mathematical community, and AI will have to continue to prove itself in the face of skepticism.

Meanwhile, I would use my own countermeasures to ensure that my AI systems circumvent these countermeasures and remain competitive.

I think the likelihood of an AI system overruling incorrect but popular human beliefs over the next decade in the US general population 50% of the time in any of these three domains: physics, biology, or history is low. While AI systems have the potential to challenge human beliefs, they must be able to effectively communicate their reasoning and provide evidence to support their conclusions. Additionally, public acceptance of AI-assisted decision-making and the adoption of AI systems as reliable sources of information in these domains will be important. Although AI systems can process vast amounts of information and identify patterns, it may take time for humans to trust AI-generated predictions and recommendations. Therefore, I estimate the probability of an AI system overruling incorrect but popular human beliefs over the next decade in the US general population 50% of the time in any of these three domains to be around 0.25.
